title: backup_scheduler: sleep delay loses sub-second precision — cron fire can be missed
description: backup_scheduler.rs line 102: delay_secs = (next - Utc::now()).num_seconds().max(0) as u64. num_seconds() truncates, not rounds. If next is 0.9s away, delay_secs=0, tokio::time::sleep(0s) fires immediately; but the next scheduled time may not have arrived yet. On the next iteration the same fire time is re-selected and the sleep is 0 again, spinning until the second boundary passes. Not a hard bug, but causes wasted-CPU spin-wait on sub-second boundary. Should use duration_round or ceiling division: (chrono::Duration).to_std().unwrap_or_default() to get full precision Duration instead of num_seconds().
